title: After the opening: Berlin night out and sightseeing
summary: Wooding declines a Berlin brothel visit because his wife is along, then tours the Kaiser's palace and coffee-houses with big bands.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: person anyhow. Anyhow, so then we went out. Now we went to -- right away the Germans said, "Well we must take you first to a bawdy house." We went to this bawdy house. But here's what I didn't need. I'd been always respected by Lyons and all of them and I had my wife with me, so, as well as I wanted to do something in that bawdy house, I didn't. Because I wanted to keep my respect up. And I was almost slobbering at the mouth, but I still kept my respect. I said, "Oh, no, I wouldn't do it. I brought my wife all the way from America with me. I wouldn't dare to do anything like this, see."

So I was back there the next day with my own boys and we got into what trouble they didn't get that day, so see. Anyhow, so they all had a good time, but Johnny Mitchell went to -- see the other guys wasn't thinking. But, as the leader, I had to keep a certain amount of prestige up. So, but now, the Germans came in like a bunch of flies and all. The next day they grabbed us and they took us to all the places -- now this is where -- first they took us to and the droskys too, we had never seen droskys, too. You know they're something like our horse with the hansom behind.
And we went up to the (Krool) Garden, we went to the Kaiser's palace, which was a museum now. Took a

drive down Unter den Linden. And then the others went to Tier Park and then we went into the Tier Gardens, and there was a place there called Krohl Garden, which fascinated us. The Germans had these big bands playing there in these prestige coffee-houses. Sometimes something like 25 men playing in these coffee-houses. Which we don't have today. But in those days it was really a life that we didn't know and Berlin was such a beautiful place that, really, those days there, we really enjoyed.
